It's {d}damn tough {A}life full of {d}toil and {a}strife
We {d}whalermen {a}under{d}go.
And we don't give a {A}damn when the {d}gale is {a}stopped
How {B}hard the {a}wind did {d}blow.
For we're {F}homeward bound from the {C}Arctic ground
With a {d}good ship, taut and {A}free.
And we {d}don't give a {A}damn we {d}drink our {A7}rum
With the {d}girls of {a}old {d}Maui.

Ref: Rolling {F}down to Old Maui{C},  me boys
Rolling {B}down to Old Maui{A},
We're {d}homeward {A}bound from the {d}Arctic {a}ground,
Rolling {d}down to {a}Old {d}Maui.

Once more we sail with a northerly gale
Trough the ice and wind and rain.
Them coconut fronds, them tropical lands
We soon shall se again.
Six hellish months have passed away
On the cold Kamchatka Sea.
But now we're bound from the Arctic ground,
Rolling down to Old Maui.

Once more we sail with a northerly gale
Towards our island home.
Our mainmast sprung, our whaling done,
And we ain't got far to roam.
Our stuns'l bones is carried away,
What care we for that sound?
A living gale is after us,
Thank God we're homeward bound.

How soft the breeze through the islands trees,
Now the ice is far astern.
Them native maids, them tropical glades
Are a-waiting our return.
Even now their big brown eyes look out
Hoping some fine day to see 
Our baggy sails runnin '   'fore the gales
Rolling down to old Maui.
title: Rolling Down To Old Maui
